facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: It would appear that the site was settled in the 3rd century B.C. at the time that the emperor Asoka, the grandson of Chandragupta, who had defeated the Macedonian invaders and founded the Maurya dynasty, was converted to Buddhism.
facts.text: The Great Stupa at Sanchi was originally commissioned by Mauryan Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE as a brick hemispherical dome covering relics of the Buddha.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Since the fourteenth century Sanchi remained deserted and uncared for till 1818 when General Taylor rediscovered the site.
facts.text: British cavalry officer General Henry Taylor documented and brought modern archaeological attention to the abandoned ruins of Sanchi in 1818.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: In 1822, Maddock clumsily breached the Great Stupa at Sanchi, although he was not able to reach the center, and he then abandoned.
facts.text: In 1822, British political agent Herbert Maddock breached the dome of the Great Stupa from top to foundation while hunting for treasure, causing extensive structural destruction.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Sir John Marshall established an archaeological museum in 1919, which was later transformed into the present site museum at Sanchi.
facts.text: Between 1912 and 1919, Director General of Archaeology Sir John Marshall carried out the systematic reconstruction and conservation of Sanchi, financially supported by Sultan Jahan Begum of Bhopal.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The original brick stupa was encased in a stone facing that nearly doubled its diameter to 36.6 metres and increased its height to 16.5 metres.
facts.text: The outer stone casing expanded the Great Stupa to a diameter of 36.6 metres and a dome height of 16.46 metres.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: An inscription on the Southern Gateway records that it was executed by the ivory carvers of Vidisha.
facts.text: A dedicatory Brahmi inscription on the Southern Gateway reveals that its stone carvings were made by the guild of ivory carvers from Vidisha.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The pillar bears an edict of Ashoka warning against schism in the Buddhist church.
facts.text: The Ashokan pillar erected near the Southern Gateway bears an edict declaring that any monk or nun who breaks the unity of the Buddhist order shall be expelled from the Sangha.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: While halting at the city of Vedisa, he dwelt in the house of a merchant and won the hand of his daughter, the noble lady Devi.
facts.text: The Sri Lankan chronicle Mahavamsa states that Emperor Ashoka married Devi, a merchant's daughter from Vidisha, who founded the monastery at Vedisagiri near modern Sanchi.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: King Asoka took the relics of the Buddha, had eighty-four thousand caskets made of gold, silver, crystal, and lapis lazuli, and distributed them among eighty-four thousand stupas.
facts.text: The Sanskrit Buddhist narrative Ashokavadana records that Emperor Ashoka redistributed bodily relics from seven pre-existing stupas into 84,000 stupas across his empire.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: Susan Huntington challenged the traditional aniconic interpretation of early Buddhist art, arguing that scenes previously read as life events of the Buddha actually depict worship of sacred spots and relic shrines.
facts.text: Art historians disagree over the narrative panels of Sanchi, where Alfred Foucher asserted that empty thrones and riderless horses signified a strict doctrinal ban on depicting the Buddha's physical body, whereas Susan Huntington argued these reliefs represent historical pilgrimage worship of sacred shrines rather than aniconic life events.

facts.label: legend
facts.quote: Local tradition often claims that the stupa marks the exact site of Ashoka's wedding to Devi of Vidisha, though archaeological epigraphy provides no such record.
facts.text: Local lore recounts that Ashoka deliberately chose Sanchi hill because it served as the wedding venue where he married Queen Devi, though no contemporary Mauryan inscription identifies her at the site.

scenes.label: archaeology

visual.prompt: end_smile

scenes.vo: Agli baar hum chalenge samundar ke neeche, Dwarka ki khoj par. Wahan gotakhor hain, yaani paani ke andar utarkar khoj karne wale log. Wahan bhi granth hain aur behas bhi. Tab tak comment mein bataiye. Aapko kya lagta hai, Sanchi stupa ke beech mein Buddha ki asthiyan thi ya nahi?

thumbnail.name: SANCHI
thumbnail.scene: The giant stone dome of the Sanchi stupa at stormy dusk with a deep jagged hole torn into its top, broken stones tumbling down the side and a lantern glowing deep inside the dark breach.

script.title: Sanchi Stupa ke andar *asthiyan* thi? 🤯

hooks: 2,300 saal purana stupa jise angrezon ne phir se joda?
Sanchi ke darwazon par kaun si kahaniyan?
